name: The Turkish Hazel of the Hortus

location.address: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam, Plantage Middenlaan 2A, 1018 DD Amsterdam (exact spot within the garden not confirmed)

access: Paid entry, Hortus Botanicus ticket required
transport: Tram 14, Artis stop, directly outside (same stop as the Hortus's already-published cycad, ams_005)
verify_notes: Planted 1795 in the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam (same garden that already hosts ams_005, the Palm House cycad, so this is a second, separate entry in the same garden). Bomenstichting (the Dutch tree foundation) records it as the oldest and thickest Turkish hazel in the Netherlands, current girth 300 cm. Registered in the national monumental trees database (monumentalebomen.nl, entry 1686149), which functions as one official-register source. NVBT (the Dutch association of botanical gardens) independently confirms Corylus colurna stands in this garden, corroborating species and presence, but not the specific 1795 planting date or 300 cm girth, which trace to a single lineage of sources (Bomenstichting content that the national register entry appears to reuse) rather than two fully independent confirmations. No dated recent sighting/photo found to confirm it is alive today, though the Hortus is a professionally maintained, continuously open botanical garden with the tree still listed in its living collections as of the most recent search, which is reasonable circumstantial evidence rather than proof. Flagged for: (1) age/girth resting on effectively one source lineage rather than two independent ones, (2) no exact in-garden coordinate found, only the garden's street address, so location_precision is approximate, garden-level. Species blooms with male catkins in January; native to Asia Minor and the Balkans. Age note: 1795 planting makes it roughly 231 years old in 2026, one of the oldest living trees in Amsterdam by planting date, though several trees on named registers elsewhere in the city are claimed older; do not present it as the city's single oldest without a citywide comparison. Remarkable angle for the writer: oldest and thickest of its species in the whole of the Netherlands, growing in a garden (Hortus, founded 1638) that has been cultivating rare and difficult plants for nearly 400 years, a few minutes' walk from the already-published wingnut and cycad, so it slots straight into the existing Plantage cluster without adding any distance to the walk.
